arxiv-2110-03109.title: Consistent Counterfactuals for Deep Models
arxiv-2110-03109.creator: Emily BlackDepartment of Computer ScienceCarnegie Mellon UniversityPittsburgh, PA 15213, USA emilybla@cs.cmu.edu, Zifan Wang Department of Electrical and Computer EngineeringCarnegie Mellon UniversityPittsburgh, PA 15213, USA zifanw@cmu.edu Matt FredriksonDepartment of Computer ScienceCarnegie Mello
arxiv-2110-03109.description: Abstract Counterfactual examples are one of the most commonly-cited methods for explaining the predictions of machine learning models in key areas such as finance and medical diagnosis. Counterfactuals are often discussed under the assumption that the model on which they will be used is static, but in deployment models may be periodically retrained or fine-tuned.

arxiv-2208-05796.title: Rotating hairy black holes and thermodynamics from gravitational decoupling
arxiv-2208-05796.creator: Subhash Mahapatra, Indrani Banerjee
arxiv-2208-05796.description: Abstract We study the method of extended gravitational decoupling in obtaining static black hole solutions satisfying Einstein’s equations with a tensor vacuum. The source has quite generic characteristics and satisfies the strong energy condition. The stationary, axisymmetric counterpart of the static metric is obtained by applying the Newman-Janis and Azreg-Aïnou algorithms.

arxiv-2209-09159.title: Transition Amplitudes in 3D Quantum Gravity: Boundaries and Holography in the Coloured Boulatov Model
arxiv-2209-09159.creator: Christophe Goeller, Daniele Oriti, Gabriel Schmid
arxiv-2209-09159.description: Abstract We consider transition amplitudes in the coloured simplicial Boulatov model for three-dimensional Riemannian quantum gravity. First, we discuss aspects of the topology of coloured graphs with non-empty boundaries. Using a modification of the standard rooting procedure of coloured tensor models, we then write transition amplitudes systematically as topological expansions.

arxiv-2501-13090.title: Innovative Web Tool for Remote Data Acquisition and Analysis: Customized for SKA Low frequency Beamforming Test Bed LPDA Array at Gauribidanur Radio Observatory

arxiv-2501-13090.description: Abstract With the evolution of radio astronomy, related education and training, the demand for scalable, efficient, and remote systems in data acquisition, storage, and analysis has significantly increased. Addressing this need, we have developed a web interface for a log-periodic dipole antenna (LPDA) array integral to the SKA Test activities at the Gauribidanur Radio Observatory (77.428 E, 13.603 N).

arxiv-2507-01482.title: Approximation of Dirac operators with 𝜹 \boldsymbol{\delta} -shell potentials in the norm resolvent sense, II. Quantitative results
arxiv-2507-01482.creator: Jussi Behrndt, Markus Holzmann, Christian Stelzer-Landauer
arxiv-2507-01482.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jussi Behrndt, Markus Holzmann, Christian Stelzer-Landauer. This paper is devoted to the approximation of two and three-dimensional Dirac operators H V ~ ​ δ Σ H_{\widetilde{V}\delta_{\Sigma}} with combinations of electrostatic and Lorentz scalar δ \delta -shell interactions in the norm resolvent sense. Relying on results from [ 8 ] an explicit smallness condition on the coupling parameters is derived so that H V ~ ​ δ Σ H_{\widetilde{V}\delta_{\Sigma}} is the limit of Dirac operators with scaled electrostatic and Lorentz scalar potentials.

arxiv-2509-17083.title: HyRF: Hybrid Radiance Fields for Memory-efficient and High-quality Novel View Synthesis
arxiv-2509-17083.creator: Zipeng Wang, Dan Xu
arxiv-2509-17083.description: Abstract Recently, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a powerful alternative to NeRF-based approaches, enabling real-time, high-quality novel view synthesis through explicit, optimizable 3D Gaussians. However, 3DGS suffers from significant memory overhead due to its reliance on per-Gaussian parameters to model view-dependent effects and anisotropic shapes.

arxiv-2601-22787.title: Float8@2bits: Entropy Coding Enables Data-Free Model Compression
arxiv-2601-22787.creator: Patrick Putzky, Martin Genzel, Mattes Mollenhauer, Sebastian Schulze, Thomas Wollmann, Stefan Dietzel
arxiv-2601-22787.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Patrick Putzky, Martin Genzel, Mattes Mollenhauer, Sebastian Schulze, Thomas Wollmann, Stefan Dietzel. Post-training compression is currently divided into two contrasting regimes. On the one hand, fast, data-free, and model-agnostic methods (e.g., NF4 or HQQ) offer maximum accessibility but suffer from functional collapse at extreme bit-rates below 4 bits. On the other hand, techniques leveraging calibration data or extensive recovery training achieve superior fidelity but impose high computational constraints and face uncertain robustness under data distribution shifts.

pmc-12429750.title: A Prospective Analysis of Scapular Positioning Patterns and Shoulder and Elbow Injury Susceptibility in Professional Baseball Pitchers
pmc-12429750.creator: Kevin Laudner, Regan Wong, Keith Meister, Yuji Uchio, Thomas M Grupp
pmc-12429750.description: Background/Objectives: Baseball pitchers accumulate extreme upper extremity forces during the repetitive, high-velocity motion of throwing, which can lead to shoulder dysfunction and overuse injuries. Although scapular dyskinesis has been linked to various shoulder pathologies, there is a lack of evidence on the specific scapular patterns predisposing pitchers to injury.

pmc-12530643.title: Bridging the Infodemic Equity Gap: North-South Digital Health Disparities and a Framework for Action
pmc-12530643.creator: Augustus Osborne
pmc-12530643.description: Rapidly propagating false and misleading health claims do not strike all societies evenly. Structural digital inequalities, uneven platform governance leverage, gaps in multilingual health literacy, and divergent political information climates have combined to produce what is argued here as an infodemic equity gap: a patterned disparity in exposure to, resilience against, and recoverability from health misinformation between and within countries.
